body: You can't predict, but you can prepare: estimate where the market is in its cycle and adjust aggression gradually. Marks's 'temperature' inputs: investor psychology (greed vs fear), credit availability and lending standards, issuance quality (IPOs of loss-making or tiny firms), valuation vs history, and the prevailing narrative ('this time is different'). Indian temperature checklist: smallcap/midcap P/E premium to Nifty; mainboard and SME IPO counts and subscription multiples; retail F&O volumes and new demat additions; market cap/GDP (above ~120% = hot, below ~70% = cold, per 2008/2020/2024 history); NBFC/corporate bond spreads; FPI positioning and the rupee. Posture rule: in hot readings, raise quality, trim small caps, keep dry powder; in cold readings, deploy in steps. Second-level thinking: ask what consensus expects and what is priced, not just whether a company is good. Limitation: temperature readings are early by months or years.
title: Marks: market temperature and stepwise risk posture
